local_math_contract: For a point at the circle center, every point on the arc is equally distant: return an outward interval for the radius.
For a noncentral point whose radial direction belongs to the directed interval, the closest circle point lies in the interval; bound the absolute difference of point radius and circle radius.

Otherwise a nearest point on a closed directed interval is one of its two endpoints. Bound each endpoint squared distance via norm(point-center)^2 + radius^2 - 2 dot(point-center,ray)*sqrt(radius^2/norm(ray)^2), respecting the dot-product sign. Take interval minima then outward square roots.
Use exact rational cross/dot signs for angular membership and integer square-root bounds for radicals. No floating trig or tolerance epsilon may decide membership or narrow a certificate.
Irrational endpoint coordinates must not be replaced by rounded points. Resource exhaustion is explicit, never an approximate success.
